# R parity golden values

Golden intermediate values frozen from the R DENR reference implementation.
Each `<scenario>.json` corresponds to a scenario in `tests/fixtures/scenarios.py`
and is consumed by `tests/test_parity.py`.

**This directory is empty until Phase 0 is done.** The parity tests skip with an
actionable message when a golden file is missing, and
`test_parity_coverage_is_reported` prints how many scenarios remain unverified —
so a fully skipped parity suite does not read as success.

## Producing them

Inputs are generated by us, not copied from the R package, because its
`LICENSE.md` (MIT) and `DESCRIPTION` (GPL >=2) disagree about redistribution.
What lands here is R *program output*, which is safe to commit.

```bash
# 1. Generate the scenario inputs.
uv run python -m tests.fixtures.generate --output build/parity-inputs

# 2. Run the export inside the reference environment. The DENR README publishes
#    a container, which is the frozen environment plan Phase 0 calls for.
singularity pull library://rhassett-cshl/stadyum/denr:latest
singularity exec denr_latest.sif Rscript scripts/export_r_golden.R \
    --inputs build/parity-inputs \
    --output tests/fixtures/parity \
    --commit 09d6cde5ef7ad1a6eb140c6e25dbae91e2a9a819
```

Pass `--commit` so each golden records which DENR revision produced it; the
Python side reports it when a comparison fails.

A local R also works, but needs the Bioconductor stack (`GenomicRanges`,
`GenomicFeatures`, `rtracklayer`, `AnnotationDbi`) plus DENR itself. The
container is preferred precisely because it pins those versions.

## What is compared

Per plan section 13: locus membership, bin boundaries, mask indices, the reduced
design matrix, transcript-to-model equivalence classes, binned signal, predicted
signal and objective (everywhere, including rank-deficient loci), and fitted
abundance (only on full-rank loci, where it is unique).
